audit.why: 54.85% over 505 games against a diffRating of 7.5/10 is a little pessimistic, but the mirror settled the tags and the lane genuinely swings — Kennen owns the shuriken window and level 6, Olaf owns 4-5 and two items. Not worth fighting the mirror over.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers agreed with each other but not with the packet or the already-applied mirror. Page had Kennen,Skill,Olaf,Olaf,Kennen,Olaf,Olaf; packet and mirror both give Skill,Kennen,Skill,Olaf,Kennen,Skill,Olaf.
audit.why: The mirror (kennen__olaf) is already on disk with the packet order, so mirror-fix.js would overwrite four rows here anyway. Rows 1 and 2 in particular were backwards: the page's own whys[1] calls levels 2-3 'his poke peak', which cannot be an Olaf row.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 1, 2 and 5 flipped as matched full/content pairs to Skill, Kennen, Skill, Skill; ratings on those rows rescaled to 5/4/5/5. whys[0] and whys[5] reworded so the prose stops claiming Olaf owns rows that are now Skill.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three strings credit Olaf's W with sustain ('W-omnivamp', 'W-sustain'). Riot's W text is 'Olaf's Attack Speed is increased and he gains a Shield' — the lifesteal is Berserker Rage, the passive, scaling with MISSING health. Separately, no Kennen cooldown appears anywhere: Lightning Rush is 10/9/8/7/6s and Slicing Maelstrom is a flat 120s at every rank, which is the single most exploitable number in the lane.
audit.why: The W/passive mix-up changes the decision: a shield says disengage after it pops, missing-health lifesteal says stay in and swing. And 'engage on his ult cooldown' is unusable advice without the 120s — that is a two-minute window in which Kennen cannot answer an all-in at all. The decisive interaction is right and stays: Ragnarok makes Olaf immune to disables while he keeps attacking, so Mark of the Storm's triple-mark stun does not land through it.
audit.corrected: Berserker Rage named in whys[3], spikes[2].text and content.mid. Lightning Rush's 10s and Slicing Maelstrom's flat 120s written into dosFull[0].d, breakdown.cooldowns and phases[4].why. spikes[1].text now names Mark of the Storm and Slicing Maelstrom rather than 'his ult'.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page tracks Lightning Rush as the matchup-defining cooldown. The genuinely punishable one is Slicing Maelstrom at 120s flat.
audit.why: Lightning Rush is a 6-10s escape — you cannot plan a lane around a cooldown that short. The 120s ult is the window that decides whether an all-in works.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns now tracks both, with Slicing Maelstrom's 120s named. focus.text left as Lightning Rush to stay consistent with the mirror and the ~12 other strings keyed to it.

So bait it — once his ult is on cooldown, OR pop your own Ragnarok as the stun lands so it never roots you, then E his face for the true-damage chunk. At 6 with R up, a Kennen with no peel and no flash is just dead.

notes: Both layers already agreed with each other here, so this was not a two-layer split — the shared chart was simply the wrong order versus the packet and the already-applied mirror, on four of seven rows.
